title: INTERIM REPORT on the proposal for a Council regulation laying down the Multiannual Financial Framework for the years 2028 to 2034
part_text: 125. Rejects the Commission’s proposal for a novel crisis mechanism based on extraordinary joint borrowing backed by additional headroom under the own resources ceiling; considers that joint borrowing, even if temporary and strictly regulated, entails significant budgetary and financial risks, and sets a precedent that could weaken the Union’s budgetary discipline in the long term; stresses that tying such mechanisms to the EU budget’s credit rating exposes it to greater financial commitments, to the detriment of the MFF’s long-term sustainability; considers that the proliferation of instruments based on common debt makes the budget less transparent and undermines political accountability; recalls that the Union’s capacity to react to crises must be based, first and foremost, on internal reallocation, better prioritisation and rigorous use of existing instruments, rather than creating new forms of common debt;
